team.name: dream-team
team.description: Stack-agnostic multi-agent development team for Claude Code. Invoke with /team <task>.

modelRouting._comment: The model for each Agent call: the cell for its workflow and call (by the task's Complexity where the cell is low/medium/high), one tier up when the orchestrator judged the run hard, then raised to the role's floor and capped at the session model; the ceiling wins over the floor. ceiling = the session model, passed by omitting model, which is why every agent file declares model: inherit. A call key's suffix marks a second kind of call to one role (researcher-explorer:wide = the wide research pass, reviewer:final = the review of the whole diff, reviewer:diagnose = the diagnosis a linked run opens with after a developer reports a defect in a closed run, and the verification of review comments and complaints about delivered code, skills/team/references/review-comments.md); its floor is the role's. Layout is read line by line: each workflow opens on its own line, one call per line, a low/medium/high object inline. Bug Fix, Small Change and Quick Fix carry a tester cell for the test a fix sometimes needs; full_feature carries a doc-writer cell for its documentation-only tasks. The change-reviewer call is the independent review of a finished change: the whole of Review Changes, and the final pass of a code-changing run (skills/team/references/final-pass.md).

budgets._comment: Checked at four characters to one token; no tokenizer is available to the skills that read this. A file listed in overrides is measured against its own number instead of the default for its class. The learnings index is no file: knowledge.learningsIndex prints it from the entry files, one row per entry, the title cut to learningsIndexRowTitleChars and the tags to learningsIndexRowMaxTags, and checks/verify-learnings-inbox.sh reports /generate-knowledge due past learningsIndexMaxRows rows. learningsTrapAgeDays: a kept trap older than this, with no mark, is offered for promotion by the generator's triage when the index holds learningsIndexMaxRows minus two rows or more. proposalsMaxFiles: with more files than this under proposalsDir, waiting for a refresh, knowledge.drift says a refresh is due.

classification._comment: subset = a reader needs part of it, so it becomes an index at this path plus a sibling directory of topics. whole = every reader needs all of it, so it stays one file and is cut, never split.

covers._comment: What each required file's Covers: line declares, and the default knowledge.drift applies to a file, or a topic of its index, that has none. paths = the file describes code at git glob pathspecs and is marked when one of them changed since the baseline commit. conventions = the file describes how code is written, never marked by path.

CAPABILITIES.md.note: Describes this machine, not this repository: which optional capabilities are installed and how the team may use them. Rewritten by every /team-setup run. Absent or empty means the team runs with none, which is a supported state.

tracking._comment: Run state shared by every edition of the team. Teams before 4.0.0 kept it in legacyDir; tools/migrate-tracking.sh moves it, run by /team-setup when its dry run is clean.

amendments._comment: Team amendments: lessons about the team itself, kept per project and applied by the running team until the team absorbs them (skills/team/references/amendments.md). The collector lives in run state, which survives git pull inside .claude/ and is never committed; the resolution list ships with the team and is where the lead records each amendment adopted, declined or superseded. maxActive only makes the final report ask for the collector to be sent to the lead; it never blocks an entry. maxPerClose caps the consent question at one run's close. The Verifier's amendment and retire calls use the run's verifier cell, or the verifier floor where the workflow has none (Analyze, Docs, or Step -1 before a workflow is fixed).

update._comment: The supported install is a clone in place: .claude/ is a checkout of this repository, and /team-setup fetches it and pulls when it is behind and clean. A copy still works; setup then shows the copy command instead. Nothing contacts the network except git against the remote the user cloned from.

postUpdate._comment: Keyed by the version that introduced the step. /team-setup compares the record's lastVersion with team.version and applies every step of every version above it, oldest first, then writes the record; a missing record applies them all. A do step is performed by setup itself; knowledge steps are named in one report line, because /generate-knowledge is a command only the user starts.

hooks.purpose: Sticky team mode: while the marker file says state=open, every user prompt is routed back through the /team orchestrator, surviving model switches, pauses, compaction and restarts; while it says state=closed, every prompt is triaged as feedback on the run that just closed (skills/team/references/follow-up.md); the guard denies destructive shell commands only while a run is open, except commands listed verbatim in TOOLCHAIN.md.
hooks.requires: a bash shell (Git Bash or WSL on Windows); without one both hooks exit quietly: sticky mode is unavailable and the guard denies nothing

pluginPolicy.consent: Every plugin in this list is optional and is installed only after the user agrees to that specific plugin. /team-setup reports what is missing and asks once, in one multi-select, which of the missing ones to install. /team and the subagents never install, enable or disable a plugin.
pluginPolicy.degradation: The team must produce the same quality of work with none of these installed. A capability is an accelerator, never a prerequisite. An agent that cannot see a capability proceeds without it and never tells the user something was impossible because a plugin was absent.
pluginPolicy.brokering: Subagents run with the tool list in their own frontmatter, which does not include tools contributed by plugins. By default the orchestrator uses a capability itself and passes the result into the handoff. A team owner who wants an agent to call a capability directly must add that capability's tools to the agent's frontmatter; /team-setup reports which agents would need that and never edits them.
pluginPolicy.verification: Install identifiers below were confirmed against the official marketplace listing and the vendors' own installation instructions in September 2026. Re-check before relying on one; /team-setup reports what is actually installed rather than trusting this file.

plugins.name: context7
plugins.alternativeInstall: claude mcp add --scope user context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp
plugins.useWhen: The task depends on a third-party library or framework and the exact current signature, option name, or version-specific behaviour is not visible in this repository. Look it up before designing or writing the call, not after it fails.
plugins.neverUseFor: Anything about this project's own code, conventions or commands — those come from the project knowledge and the repository itself. Fetched documentation never overrides an observed project convention; when they disagree, the repository wins and the disagreement is reported.

plugins.name: claude-mem
plugins.install: /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem, then /plugin install claude-mem
plugins.detect: a tool or command whose name contains "mem", contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At preflight, to recall the user's standing preferences and what earlier sessions concluded about this project. Treat every recollection as a hint to verify, never as a fact.
plugins.neverUseFor: Storing the team's own learnings. LEARNINGS.md stays the team's one inbox of project traps on their way to becoming rules: it is reviewable, project-scoped and lives beside the code. Never let a recollection outrank the repository or the knowledge files.

plugins.name: claude-md-management
plugins.detect: a command for revising the project instruction file, contributed by this plugin
plugins.useWhen: At the docs-sync step of a run that changed a documented rule or created a new obligation: propose the instruction-file update through this capability and let the user approve the diff.
plugins.neverUseFor: Editing project instruction files silently or in the middle of a run, and regenerating PROJECT-RULES.md — that belongs to the knowledge generator, which reads the instruction file rather than writing it.

plugins.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
plugins.detect: a tool for navigating, inspecting or screenshotting a live browser page
plugins.useWhen: A run changed something a person sees and the result can be observed by loading the running application: the Tester needs a check against real rendering, the Reviewer needs to confirm the change actually appears, or a diagnosis needs the real console or network behaviour. The Designer needs to see the pages of its surface before an audit or a brief.
plugins.neverUseFor: Projects with no user interface; starting a server or opening a page without the user agreeing first; and never as a substitute for a test — a screenshot is evidence, not coverage.

plugins.name: playwright
plugins.marketplace: (not published as a marketplace plugin as of September 2026)
plugins.detect: a tool for driving a browser through structured page data
plugins.useWhen: Same as the other browser-control entry. Install at most one of the two: two browser drivers competing for the same page waste context and produce contradictory observations.
plugins.neverUseFor: Same exclusions as the other browser-control entry.

checks.runFrom: the team root: this repository, or .claude/ in a project the team is deployed into
checks.note: "hook" is deliberately absent from this pattern: it is a Claude Code harness term the team must be able to name. React's hooks are caught by useState/useEffect instead.
checks.stackNeutralityLint: grep -n -i -E "\b(go|golang|python|java|c#|csharp|dotnet|typescript|javascript|node|react|angular|vue|redux|usestate|useeffect|selector|slice|controller|mediatr|cqrs|linq|dbcontext|prisma|sqlalchemy|xunit|nunit|jest|vitest|pytest|npm|pip|nuget|cargo|csproj|axios|fetch|swagger|openapi|gofmt|eslint|prettier|nullable|eager.?load|n\+1|re-?render|functional component|any types|router)\b" agents/*.md skills/*/SKILL.md skills/team/references/*.md templates/review-baseline.md README.md
checks.knowledgeIntegrityArgs: <backup-dir> <dir> [inbox], in that order, once per pair: the backup's knowledge/ with the resolver's project dir; its operative/ only through inbox.sh verify-backup <backup-dir>/operative, which passes the inbox itself and the third argument inbox, never a path a role types; inbox compares only LEARNINGS.md and learnings/, ignores every other entry, and passes when both directories are absent; exit 0 means every guarantee held
checks.knowledgeIntegrityRunFrom: the project root, not .claude/: the path arguments are project-root-relative, so prefix each script path with .claude/; one run per pair — bash .claude/checks/verify-knowledge-integrity.sh .dream-team-tracking/knowledge-backup-<stamp>/knowledge "$(bash .claude/tools/knowledge-dir.sh project)", then, only when the backup has operative/, bash .claude/tools/inbox.sh verify-backup .dream-team-tracking/knowledge-backup-<stamp>/operative
checks.learningsInboxArgs: <operative-dir>; exit 0 = inbox clean, 1 = /generate-knowledge is due, 2 = could not read what it needs
checks.knowledgeScaffoldArgs: <project-dir> <knowledge-dir>, in that order; exit 0 = nothing to say, 1 = scaffold knowledge and the project has content (regeneration due), 2 = a path could not be read, 3 = scaffold knowledge and the project is still empty
checks.knowledgeScaffoldRunFrom: the project root, not .claude/: both arguments are project-root-relative, the second the resolver's project dir, so prefix the script path with .claude/ — bash .claude/checks/verify-knowledge-scaffold.sh . "$(bash .claude/tools/knowledge-dir.sh project)"
checks.knowledgeNeutralArgs: <knowledge-dir>; exit 0 = no team path named, 1 = lines listed, 2 = unreadable
checks.knowledgeNeutralRunFrom: the project root: bash .claude/checks/verify-knowledge-neutral.sh <the resolver's project dir>
checks.knowledgeShapeArgs: <knowledge-dir>; exit 0 = in shape, 1 = lines listed, 2 = unreadable
